question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the cosecant-cotangent identity 

$$
1+{cot}^{2}⁡x={csc}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic cosecant-cotangent identity

$$
{coth}^{2}⁡x-1={csch}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\frac{{coth}^{4}⁡x-1}{1+{coth}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\frac{({coth}^{2}⁡x-1)({coth}^{2}⁡x+1)}{1+{coth}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}({coth}^{2}⁡x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}{csch}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{coth}⁡x\,{|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡4} \\  & =-\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡4)+\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}-1}+\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-1} \\  & =-\frac{17}{15}+\frac{5}{4} \\  & =\frac{7}{60}\end{aligned}
$$
